errors.problem: Still there from round 2. When the first term of an iḍāfa ends in tāʾ marbūṭa and carries no case vowel, the ⟶ line drops the -t that is always pronounced in construct (and that ALA-LC writes): قِطْعَة كَعْك → 'qiṭʿa kaʿk' (qiṭʿat kaʿk), ثَلَاثَة دَنَانِير → 'Thalātha danānīr' (thalāthat), بِعَشَرَة جُنَيْهَات → 'bi-ʿashara junayhāt' (bi-ʿasharat), خَمْسَة أَرْغِفَة → 'Khamsa arghifa' (khamsat), Fatima's قِطْعَة كَعْك أُخْرَى → 'qiṭʿa kaʿk'. Where the Arabic has the vowel (خَمْسَةُ أَرْغِفَة → khamsatu) it comes out right.
errors.fix: engine: romanise a vowel-less construct tāʾ marbūṭa as -t (qiṭʿat kaʿk, thalāthat danānīr); or add the case vowel in the Arabic (قِطْعَةُ كَعْكٍ وَاحِدَة)

summary: I read all 3,031 lines of audit/scenarios-1.txt: 16 scenarios (cafe to weather-plans), each with dialogue, segs, mistakes, quizzes and photo-scene spots. I checked 586 Arabic strings (harakat, case endings after verbs, kāna/sayakūnu/laysa predicates, lam/lan/an/li- moods and prohibitives, imperatives to men and women, number-noun polarity and case with جُنَيْه، رَغِيف، كَعْكَة، دَقِيقَة، مِلْعَقَة، سَنَة، آلَاف، مِئَة, non-human plural agreement, addressee gender), all translations and quiz keys, about 1,516 seg glosses and 660 tap glosses on 390 tap lines. The Arabic itself is correct: I found no wrong case ending, conjugation, agreement, translation or answer key, and the round-1/2 fixes I could see (الْوَاحِدَة gloss, مِنْ = than and لَا = don't on mistake cards, multi-sense particles) read correctly. 13 errors (2 major, 11 minor), all in glosses or the engine. 14 tap glosses are wrong or misleading in context (covered by 11 findings), most of them round-2 findings that are still unfixed: طَوِيلَةً = 'tall (after is not)' on a kāna card and الْإِشَارَة = 'pointing' on the traffic-light spot (both major), plus مَرَّةً، وَهُوَ، تَفَضَّلْ/تَفَضَّلِي (3), هُوَ، الْجَبَل (2), مَقْهَى and a new one, السَّاعَة on the clock spot. No seg gloss was wrong. Two engine patterns: the construct tāʾ marbūṭa still romanised without -t, and the new clitic-hyphen rule applied inconsistently (wakāmīrā next to wa-miftāḥu, liʾadʿuwaka, Bi-kami/bikami in one line).
